newsitem.title: GREECE: Karadzic says he innocent of war crimes in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Karadzic says he innocent of war crimes in Bosnia.

text.p: Wanted Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic told a Greek newspaper he was innocent of war crimes in Bosnia and said nobody would dare arrest him and bring him to trial.

"I have 2,000 (bodyguards) who follow me everywhere. This is why they can't arrest me and send me to the court. They know that only in a few seconds there will be 500 dead and they won't be my men," Karadzic was quoted as saying in an interview with Sunday's Eleftheros Typos newspaper.
Karadzic, twice indicted by a United Nations war crimes tribunal, is believed to be based in Pale, the self-proclaimed Bosnian Serb capital.

"I am not a war criminal. I am not guilty, to go to court," Karadzic said. "The Croats killed 700,000 Serbs in World War Two and weren't punished. Now they talk about a few hundred people who, as they say, (were probably killed) as a result of military and civilian fanaticism."
Karadzic said the Dayton agreement "was not the end of the war but just a ceasefire" and threatened to start a new war unless more territorial concessions were made to the Bosnian Serbs.
The war crimes tribunal was set up in May 1993 by the U.N. Security Council and has indicted more than 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems, for alleged war crimes. It only holds seven in custody.
